method.timing: CPU 2, current-thread runtime, one partition, 1048576 rows, batch size 8192, two warmups and nine executions per process. Physical plans are fresh for each execution. FIFO-controlled perf counters cover the same execution interval; all six counters have 100% running time. Each process contributes one median. Final settings are interleaved; each target has 16 processes per setting, other wrapped and native cases have six. No builds, memory probes, traces or validation jobs overlap final timing.
method.high_fault_group: More than 1000 faults over nine executions, used only to classify the two traced target query modes. Do not generalize the label to other SQL.
method.memory: Four processes per setting per case. Read /proc/PID/smaps_rollup and status while the child is blocked on its existing FIFO before and after execution. Context, input tables and plans are still alive. Private_Dirty is the total process private dirty memory, not an isolated cache-size measurement. VmHWM includes startup and validation. No probe timing is used for performance comparisons.
method.traces: Two processes per setting per target; only brk/mmap/munmap/madvise between enable and disable are counted. All traced timings are excluded from the untraced comparison.
method.validation: Both chosen settings preserve all 48 wrapped, 48 native-output, 20 cast and 12 Float64 captures. Full-value expectations run inside the benchmark. The earlier error corpora, Arrow unit suite and Delta lifecycle were not rerun for an environment-only change.

findings: The default allocator still produces 2/16 high-fault SMALLINT and 7/16 high-fault BIGINT processes, taking about 5.4-5.5 ms. The tcache setting produces 0/16 for each target, with process medians in 2.406-2.482 ms across both targets.

All four target tcache traces contain zero brk, mmap, munmap or madvise calls in the execution interval. Default high-fault traces show 2304 brk calls; trim-only tuning instead causes 1152 mmap and 1152 munmap calls.

Setting both mmap and trim thresholds to 1 MiB also removes the sampled target slow mode. Setting only one threshold or both to 256 KiB does not. The tcache opt-in is one setting and preserves dynamic threshold adjustment.

Compared with default, median post-execution private dirty memory rises by 298 KiB for SMALLINT and 270 KiB for BIGINT; correlated MAX rises by 3824 KiB. These are measured workload deltas, not memory limits.

Wrapped controls range from -0.06% to -1.88% median elapsed; native controls range from -0.0004% to -0.93%. Small positive mean/outlier differences remain in the artifact. No universal performance or memory claim is made.
limitations: Measured on one glibc 2.42 Linux host. No older glibc, musl, macOS, Windows, replacement allocator or Python-host validation.
Cache retention is per thread and workload-dependent. These single-thread, in-memory runs do not bound memory in concurrent sessions or repeated workloads.
The setting changes libc allocation policy for the whole process; it is not a SQL option and cannot be silently enabled by importing a binding.
Default behavior and the previous optional patches remain unchanged. No general cross-platform allocator fix is claimed. The 126 tracked SQL compatibility differences remain open.
